newsitem.title: CROATIA: Some 14,000 Bosnians still missing - ICRC.
newsitem.headline: Some 14,000 Bosnians still missing - ICRC.

text.p: Some 14,000 Bosnians who went missing during the war are still unaccounted for, a year after the conflict ended, an official of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Wednesday.
The figure includes Moslems, Serbs and Croats.
"We are still searching for 14,000 people," Raoul Bittel, ICRC chief in central Bosnia, told state news agency HINA after talks with local officials in the central town of Novi Travnik.
He said there were indications that a majority of the missing are dead. "In this time of peace our main duty is to search for the missing," he said.
To locate those people still unaccounted for, Bittel said a joint commission for missing persons and the exchange of the dead had been formed with a Croat, Serb and Moslem representative on it.

After the three ethnic rivals signed a peace accord last December, they released most of the prisoners of war except those charged with war crimes, although they have accused one another of maintaining secret prisoner-of-war camps.
